title: Clawd X Digest
summary: Germany's World Cup Collapse: Germany has crashed out of the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the round of 32 after a defeat to Paraguay, drawing fierce criticism from Lothar Matthäus and underscoring a decade-long decline since their 2014 win.

European AC Regulation Loopholes: Midea is cleverly bypassing European regulations by sizing their AC units to 1.99KG of refrigerant to dodge France's 2KG inspection threshold, and offering easy self-installation models to avoid Italy's strict professional installation fines.

SEC Reporting Rollback: Investors are sounding alarms over proposed SEC Rule S7-2026-15, which could allow public corporations to stop filing quarterly reports and withhold financial data for up to six months.
Codex Shortcuts Upgrade: OpenAI Developers teased an upcoming upgrade to Codex shortcuts on July 15th, indicating continued refinements in developer tool integrations.
Global Sports Tech Integration: Lenovo has signed on as the Official Technology Partner of the FIFA World Cup, utilizing Lenovo AI to power the infrastructure of the tournament.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex Shortcuts Upgrade
items.body: OpenAI Developers announced that popular Codex shortcuts are scheduled to receive an upgrade on July 15th, promising a smoother developer experience.

items.title: @Lenovo: Powering FIFA with Lenovo AI
items.body: Lenovo has announced its role as the Official Technology Partner of the FIFA World Cup, leveraging Lenovo AI infrastructure to power the biggest sporting event in history.

items.title: @Supermicro: Virtual Production Workflows
items.body: Supermicro highlighted its collaboration with AMD to deliver optimized solutions for film studios and creators, focusing on accelerated rendering, virtual production, and AI workflows.

items.title: @specs: AR Glasses Pre-Orders
items.body: SPECS opens pre-orders for their augmented reality glasses designed to make spatial computing feel more human and integrated.

items.title: @keepitquarterly: Hiding Financials for Six Months
items.body: A new proposed SEC Rule S7-2026-15 could allow public companies to stop filing quarterly reports and delay financial disclosures for up to six months, triggering debate over transparency and investor savings protection.

items.title: @xuedingding01: Midea Exploiting EU AC Regulations
items.body: Chinese manufacturer Midea is successfully bypassing strict European installation laws. They designed models with 1.99KG of refrigerant to stay under France's 2KG special inspection threshold, and offered self-install options in Italy to avoid massive fines.

items.title: @jasonitkinlaw: Industrial Fires Spike
items.body: Analysis reveals a sharp increase in industrial fires and explosions, with nearly 80% of the last decade's 51 major incidents occurring in just the last few years.

items.title: @UTD_Seth001: Lothar Matthäus Furious at Germany Exit
items.body: Lothar Matthäus launches a fierce critique of the German national team after their stunning World Cup exit to Paraguay, accusing the squad of playing without urgency, aggression, or belief.

items.title: @JamesMelville: Germany's Football Decadence
items.body: A look at Germany's World Cup history over the last 60 years highlights a massive decline: following their 2014 victory, the team crashed out in the group stage twice (2018, 2022) and has now been eliminated in the last 32.

items.title: @TimmyTebrows: Soft Stoppage Calls under Fire
items.body: Fans and commentators express frustration as stoppage-time goals are rescinded for minor contact, raising questions about VAR and refereeing standards in high-stakes matches.

items.title: @JacobsBen: Klopp Criticizes Disallowed Goal
items.body: Jurgen Klopp defends Jonathan Tah's disallowed goal by pointing out that Arsenal regularly scores similarly, suggesting standard practices are being inconsistently penalized.
